desc:
There are n people labelled 0 to n - 1. Each log entry [t, a, b] records that people a and b became friends at time t. The logs come in no particular order.

Two people are acquainted at time T if they are friends by time T (their log time is at most T) or if they are linked by a chain of such friendships. Return the earliest time T at which every person is acquainted with every other person. If that never happens, return -1.

n = 4, logs = [[0,2,3],[1,0,1],[3,0,3],[4,1,2],[7,3,1]]

result = 3     (after time 3: 2-3, 0-1 and 0-3 link all four people)
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < n and a ≠ b
No pair of people appears in two logs
hints: Friendships only ever get added over time, so the groups of acquainted people only merge, never split.
Process the logs in increasing order of time and keep merging the groups of a and b.
Count groups with union-find, starting from n. When a merge brings the count down to 1, the time of the current log is the answer. If you finish all logs with more than one group, return -1.
editorial: Sort the logs by time. Maintain a union-find over the people with a counter groups = n. For each log, if the two people have different roots, merge them and decrement the counter. The first log that brings the counter to 1 gives the answer, because the state "everyone connected" is reached exactly then and not earlier. Several logs may share a time; the answer is a time value, so ties do not matter.

If the counter is still above 1 after all logs, someone is cut off, so return -1. Sorting costs O(L log L) and the unions cost O(L · α(n)), so the total is O(L log L + n). The main lesson: when a question asks when something becomes connected, sort the events by time and union them in that order.
